cases.description: Budget, payment and execution, each signed by its trusted key and bound to the frozen occurrence.
Control: every artifact is natively valid, but the execution receipt is for another occurrence of a different call.
Control: the execution receipt carries the same call content but is for a second run of that call. Matching call content is not the same execution.
The execution receipt commits to the call content and to no occurrence, so the link cannot be decided.
The payment receipt commits to no occurrence, so it could be moved to any call.
The payment receipt names a second run of the same call.
The spending limit is the agent's own statement, not the issuer's.
One bit of the issuer's signature changed.
A valid signature by a key the trust inputs do not list.
The payment is larger than what is left of the issuer's limit.
The payment names a budget statement other than the one presented.
A valid signature by a key the trust inputs do not list for the rail.
The payment signature fails while its committed occurrence is right: the native verdict and the link are separate claims.
The execution signature fails while its committed occurrence is right.
A trusted key, but trusted for the issuer role, not the responder role.
Paid, with no execution receipt.
The receipt states it audited the full three-line fixture, not the pinned two-line input. A different input digest is refused.
The receipt states the earlier version of the reference dataset, not the one the occurrence froze. A different dataset digest is refused.
The receipt states no input digest, so whether the pinned input was audited cannot be decided.
Control: paid, no reply and no statement. A bare missing reply leaves the call unresolved and the held amount held.
Paid, no reply, and the responder signs a statement naming this occurrence and saying the call did not run. The call is settled as not run.
Control: the responder's not-run statement names a second run of the same call. It says nothing about this occurrence, which stays unresolved.
The not-run statement names the call content and no occurrence, so it could be moved to any run of the call.
The payer agent, not the responder, signs that the call did not run.
One bit of the responder's not-run signature changed.
The responder signs both an execution receipt and a not-run statement for this occurrence.
